A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same A-GPS research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, appendices A–E and checklist. The relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic optimization and protein-sequence experiments, including performance curves, runtimes and ablations in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The stated off-policy sampler refresh threshold changes from 0.5S to 0.33S in Section 4.2. Equation 37 also corrects FiLM conditioning from the previous embedding e_{m-1} to the unmodified embedding e'_m. These are limited revisions to the published procedure and specification; the A-GPS framework and backbone families remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same continuous test-function configurations, Ehrlich–naturalness sequence lengths, bi-gram task and FoldX stability–SASA task. The new statement that experiments are noise-free documents existing coverage without adding a test scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same qEHVI, qNEHVI and qNParEGO comparisons, and the same VSD, CbAS, LaMBO-2 and greedy random sequence baselines and backbone variants. Newly cited evolutionary methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 revises the reported effective-sample-size refresh threshold from 0.5S to 0.33S. The 100-iteration refresh interval, experimental budgets, metrics and settings tables remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E retains the same analyses of on-policy versus off-policy gradients, gradient sample counts, prior dropout and preference-distribution parameterizations. The preference-conditioned sample visualizations are also retained; no new robustness or noise experiments appear.

E5.justification: Tables 4 and 6 retain ten synthetic-function replicates and five sequence-experiment replicates. Random-initialization descriptions, standard-deviation bands and existing table variability reporting are unchanged, with no added statistical tests or uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: The result graphics in Figures 2–4 and 7–9 are identical, and the runtime and ablation tables retain their entries and values. For example, Table 9 reports A-GPS-TFM at 6.264 (1.159) and VSD-TFM at 6.711 (0.952) in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 and Appendix B.1 explicitly introduce a noise-free assumption for the PHVI argument; v1 states only the reference-point assumption there. v3 also adds an almost-sure held-out-label argument for continuous objectives. The theorem, corollary and principal proof otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding contribution claims retain amortized preference-conditioned Pareto generation without retraining, implicit PHVI estimation, modularity and strong empirical sample efficiency. No new principal contribution or stronger performance claim is introduced.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 now distinguishes indicator equivalence on the same noisy observations from reliable statements about true objectives, and leaves noisy A-GPS convergence to future work. Section 2.2 adds the held-out-label rationale, while Section 7 adds future directions involving evolutionary quality measures and stochastic experiments.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 explicitly supplies softmax normalization for masked-transformer probabilities and clarifies the embeddings used by FiLM. Equation 19 corrects the alignment-CPE superscript, and Appendix B.1 states that all experiments are noise-free. Hardware, code access and architecture-setting tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Four references are added: Cheng et al. and Chugh et al. connect preference directions to reference-vector evolutionary methods; Afsar et al. and Rojas Gonzalez et al. support discussion of quality measures and stochastic multi-objective experiments. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized additions and corrections in the theory, architecture and discussion passages, and moves the unchanged NeurIPS checklist after the appendices. Most prose and the scientific section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The same nine figures and eleven tables are retained, with unchanged substantive graphics and table structures. Existing displays are reflowed relative to the text, particularly in Appendices C–E; these are layout changes rather than new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision through explicit qualifications of the PHVI argument, clearer noisy-objective limitations, corrected architectural expressions and acknowledgment of related reference-vector research. These address local ambiguities while preserving the empirical evidence. The revised sampling threshold is not accompanied by documented reruns, so the revision supports a modest improvement in exposition and specification, not stronger experimental validation.
